source.title: The Independence Prior of SAEs Fragments Visual Concepts
source.authors: Tommaso Mencattini; Giorgos Nikolaou; Donato Crisostomi; Thomas Fel; Francesco Montagna; E. Rodolà; Francesco Locatello

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports that standard tokenwise vision SAEs produce spatially fragmented, incomplete concept features, and that adding spatial structure improves several concept-alignment measures. This refines the claim that SAE features are complete representation units; it does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates feature-to-concept alignment and spatial coherence in synthetic data and frozen DINOv2 vision activations. It does not measure superposed directions, feature importance-based allocation, LLM feature spread, or feature dimensionality. Reconstruction-only results and spectral diagnostics are not rows for the tested version because they do not measure feature completeness. The synthetic win rates compare Spatial-SAE with matched baseline SAEs; they are not absolute recovery scores.
record.test_reason: The study argues and shows that standard tokenwise SAE features on frozen DINOv2 activations fragment visual concepts. Their maps are incomplete and spatially scattered, the class-best feature captures only part of what a linear probe decodes, and the code over-allocates high spatial frequencies. It traces this to the SAE objective's patch-independence prior. This bears on V5's claim that SAE features are complete, canonical units. Most rows, however, are win rates of the authors' own Spatial-SAE against baselines, or internal ablations. Those do not themselves measure whether SAE features are the model's units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that tokenwise SAEs implicitly impose a patch-independence prior that vision activations violate, which leaves baseline features spatially fragmented. Replacing it with a Markov-field prior (Spatial-SAE) improves synthetic concept recovery and every real-vision interpretability proxy, trading reconstruction mainly at high spatial frequencies.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a spatially regularized, two-stream SAE and tests concept recovery and spatial alignment; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method or its geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic outcomes vary with sparsifier and, in the capacity sweep, with spatial regularization strength. On ADE20K, stronger regularization can sharply reduce concept alignment; the smooth-field estimator and stream-budget allocation are also varied.

fits_no_version.finding: Vision-transformer patch activations are spatially dependent across layers: true grid neighbours explain more variance than shuffled neighbours (Figure 2). The tokenwise SAE objective implies an independent prior across patches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature fragmentation in vision models stems partly from the SAE objective's patch-independence prior, not only from the model's representation.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be publicly released upon publication.
record.problems: The real-vision experiments lack a ground-truth feature dictionary, so they use semantic alignment and interpretability proxies. Automated ratings come from Claude Haiku 4.5 rather than human raters. Several results are shown only as figures, and the paper does not test feature stability or canonical status.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction scores and graph-frequency diagnostics are not included because they do not directly measure V5 feature completeness. Detailed geometry- and capacity-sweep cells beyond the aggregate results in Table 2 are not separately recorded; those plots report comparisons across many configurations rather than individual absolute concept-feature scores.

untested.parts: No measurement of overlapping or nearly orthogonal feature geometry or of a sparsity-dependent transition. Quasi-orthogonality is only assumed as part of the LRH.
No test of whether important features get dedicated dimensions. The capacity sweep varies the superposition ratio only to compare SAE methods.
Only a vision model (DINOv2) is studied; no LLM.
Stability across seeds or runs, canonicality across SAE variants, and exhaustiveness of the dictionary are not measured.

missing.what: Concept-relative code spectra: baseline SAE codes under-allocate low graph frequencies and over-allocate high ones, with log2 ratios above 2 at the top of the spectrum. The curves nearly coincide across all four sparsifiers on both datasets. Baseline dictionaries also lack a low-frequency feature population.
missing.locator: Section 5.2; Figure 6b, 6d; Figure 15b; Appendix D.4 'A shared spectral signature'

missing.what: Absolute baseline-SAE Normalized F1 and Region Coherence for BatchTopK, Vanilla and JumpReLU on ADE20K and COCO-Stuff, readable from figure labels and Table 3. These should be recorded as baseline-SAE completeness values rather than 'figure only'.

record.verdict_notes: Most extracted rows are win rates or deltas of the authors' own method or internal ablations, so they are unlinked from V5. The V5 evidence is the characterization of baseline SAE features: qualitative fragmentation, partial Normalized F1, low coherence and the spectral excess. Real-vision results rely on proxies, since no ground-truth dictionary exists, and on a Claude Haiku 4.5 judge. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether features are represented by overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, or test a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Although synthetic experiments sweep capacity-related settings, the study does not test whether important features get dedicated dimensions while less important features share them.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Experiments concern a vision model, not LLMs.
Measures concept alignment and spatial completeness proxies, not whether SAE features are stable across runs or are canonical, exhaustive units of the representation.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Standard tokenwise SAEs (TopK, BatchTopK, Vanilla, JumpReLU) on frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 final-layer patch activations, ADE20K and COCO-Stuff
relationships.reason: Authors state the baseline features are incomplete and spatially fragmented, with holes and concepts split across atoms (r31). The spectral diagnostic shows baseline codes over-allocate high frequencies for every sparsifier on both datasets; this is from the text, not a row.
relationships.display_finding: The authors state that standard SAE features are incomplete and spatially fragmented, with holes and concepts split across atoms. A spectral diagnostic shows that standard SAE codes over-allocate high frequencies for every sparsifier on both datasets.

relationships.condition: Standard TopK SAE on DINOv2 ADE20K at expected sparsity 16
relationships.reason: The class-best baseline feature reaches only 57.5 Normalized F1 relative to a linear probe, and Region Coherence is 15.5. Changing the objective's spatial prior yields different, more concept-aligned features (65.4 and 25.9), so the features depend on the objective's prior choice (r19, r20).
relationships.display_finding: The best baseline feature per class reached only 57.5 Normalized F1 relative to a linear probe, with Region Coherence 15.5; changing the objective's spatial prior gave different, more concept-aligned features (65.4 and 25.9).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Standard tokenwise SAE features on frozen DINOv2 vision activations
reader_labels.reason: The paper explicitly describes standard SAE feature maps as incomplete and fragmented; the comparative alignment results also show lower concept alignment than Spatial-SAE (r19–r20, r31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Spatial-SAE on the tested synthetic and vision settings
reader_labels.reason: Concept-alignment and coherence proxies improve, but the study does not establish that the resulting features are stable, exhaustive, or canonical units (r1–r12, r19–r30, r32–r38).
